shloka_text: ततो जित्वा दशग्रीवो यमं त्रिदशपुङ्गवम् । रावणस्तु रणश्लाघी स्वसहायान्ददर्श ह ।। 7.23.1 ।।
transliteration: tato jitvā daśagrīvo yamaṃ tridaśapuṅgavam | rāvaṇastu raṇaślāghī svasahāyāndadarśa ha || 7.23.1 ||
translation: ततः then, जित्वा having conquered, दशग्रीवः Dashagriva, यमम् Yama, त्रिदशपुङ्गवम् the chief among the gods, रावणः Ravana, तु and, रणश्लाघी one who boasts of his prowess in battle, स्वसहायान् his own companions, ददर्श saw, ह indeed.
explanation: Then, having conquered Yama, the chief among the gods, Ravana, who boasted of his prowess in battle, indeed saw his own companions.
comments: Ravana descends to the nether ocean, subdues the Nagas at Bhogavati, and at Brahma's word makes a pact of friendship with the Nivatakavachas -- he slays the Kalakeyas and his brother-in-law Vidyujjihva, then storms Varuna's abode -- Varuna being away in Brahma's world, his sons give battle but are defeated by Ravana and his minister Mahodara -- proclaiming victory, Ravana returns toward Lanka.

shloka_text: ततो रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गं प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतम् । रावणं राक्षसा दृष्ट्वा ह्यष्टवत् समुपागमन् ।। 7.23.2 ।।
transliteration: tato rudhirasiktāṅgaṃ prahārairjarjarīkṛtam | rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasā dṛṣṭvā hyaṣṭavat samupāgaman || 7.23.2 ||
translation: ततः then, रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गम् whose body was drenched in blood, प्रहारैः by blows, जर्जरीकृतम् shattered, रावणम् Ravana, राक्षसाः the demons, दृष्ट्वा having seen, हि indeed, अष्टवत् auspiciously, समुपागमन् approached.
explanation: Then, having seen Ravana, whose body was drenched in blood and shattered by blows, the demons indeed approached him auspiciously.

shloka_text: जयेन वर्धयित्वा च मारीचप्रमुखास्ततः । पुष्पकं भेजिरे सर्वे सान्त्विता रावणेन तु ।। 7.23.3 ।।
transliteration: jayena vardhayitvā ca mārīcapramukhāstataḥ | puṣpakaṃ bhejire sarve sāntvitā rāvaṇena tu || 7.23.3 ||
translation: जयेन by victory, वर्धयित्वा having increased (celebrated), च and, मारीचप्रमुखाः Maricha and others (chiefs), ततः then, पुष्पकम् Pushpaka (chariot), भेजिरे resorted to (boarded), सर्वे all, सान्त्विताः consoled, रावणेन by Ravana, तु indeed
explanation: After Ravana had consoled them and celebrated their victory, Maricha and the other chiefs all boarded the Pushpaka chariot.

shloka_text: ततो रसातलं गच्छन् प्रविष्टः पयसां निधिम् । दैत्योरगगणाध्युष्टं वरुणेन सुरक्षितम् ।। 7.23.4 ।।
transliteration: tato rasātalaṃ gacchan praviṣṭaḥ payasāṃ nidhim | daityoragagaṇādhyuṣṭaṃ varuṇena surakṣitam || 7.23.4 ||
translation: ततः then, रसातलं Rasatala (the lowest netherworld), गच्छन् going, प्रविष्टः entered, पयसाम् of waters, निधिम् the ocean (abode), दैत्योरगगणाध्युष्टम् inhabited by hosts of Daityas and Nagas (serpents), वरुणेन by Varuna, सुरक्षितम् well-protected
explanation: Then, proceeding to Rasatala, he entered the ocean, which was inhabited by hosts of Daityas and Nagas and well-protected by Varuna.

shloka_text: स तु भोगवतीं गत्वा पुरीं वासुकिपालिताम् । कृत्वा नागान्वशे हृष्टो ययौ मणिमयीं पुरीम् ।। 7.23.5 ।।
transliteration: sa tu bhogavatīṃ gatvā purīṃ vāsukipālitām | kṛtvā nāgānvaśe hṛṣṭo yayau maṇimayīṃ purīm || 7.23.5 ||
translation: सः he, तु indeed, भोगवतीम् Bhogavati (city name), गत्वा having gone, पुरीम् city, वासुकिपालिताम् protected by Vasuki, कृत्वा having made, नागान् the Nagas (serpents), वशे under control, हृष्टः delighted, ययौ went, मणिमयीम् gem-studded, पुरीम् city
explanation: Having gone to the city of Bhogavati, protected by Vasuki, and having brought the Nagas under his control, he, delighted, proceeded to the gem-studded city.

shloka_text: निवातकवचास्तत्र दैत्या लब्धवरा वसन् । राक्षसान्तान्समागम्य युद्धाय समुपाह्वयत् ।। 7.23.6 ।।
transliteration: nivātakavacāstatra daityā labdhavarā vasan | rākṣasāntānsamāgamya yuddhāya samupāhvayat || 7.23.6 ||
translation: निवातकवचाः Nivātakavachas, तत्र there, दैत्याः Daityas, लब्धवराः who had obtained boons, वसन् lived, राक्षसान् the Rakshasa (Ravana), तान् them (the Nivātakavachas), समागम्य having approached, युद्धाय for battle, समुपाह्वयत् challenged
explanation: There lived the Nivātakavachas, Daityas who had obtained boons, and Ravana, having approached them, challenged them to battle.

shloka_text: ते तु सर्वे सुविक्रान्ता दैतेया बलशालिनः । नानाप्रहरणास्तत्र प्रहृष्टा युद्धदुर्मदाः ।। 7.23.7 ।।
transliteration: te tu sarve suvikrāntā daiteyā balaśālinaḥ | nānāpraharaṇāstatra prahṛṣṭā yuddhadurmadāḥ || 7.23.7 ||
translation: ते they, तु indeed, सर्वे all, सुविक्रान्ताः very mighty (valiant), दैतेयाः Daityas, बलशालिनः powerful, नानाप्रहरणाः having various weapons, तत्र there, प्रहृष्टाः delighted (overjoyed), युद्धदुर्मदाः intoxicated with battle (fierce in battle)
explanation: All those Daityas were indeed very mighty, powerful, equipped with various weapons, and overjoyed and fierce in battle.

shloka_text: शूलैस्त्रिशूलैः कुलिशैः पट्टिशासिपरश्वधैः । अन्योन्यं बिभिदुः क्रुद्धा राक्षसा दानवास्तथा ।। 7.23.8 ।।
transliteration: śūlaistriśūlaiḥ kuliśaiḥ paṭṭiśāsiparaśvadhaiḥ | anyonyaṃ bibhiduḥ kruddhā rākṣasā dānavāstathā || 7.23.8 ||
translation: शूलैः with spears, त्रिशूलैः with tridents, कुलिशैः with thunderbolts, पट्टिशासिपरश्वधैः with sharp-edged spears, swords, and axes, अन्योन्यं each other, बिभिदुः pierced, क्रुद्धाः enraged, राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, दानवाः the Danavas, तथा and.
explanation: The enraged Rakshasas and Danavas fiercely pierced each other with spears, tridents, thunderbolts, sharp-edged spears, swords, and axes.

shloka_text: तेषां तु युध्यमानानां साग्रः संवत्सरो गतः । न चान्यतरयोस्तत्र विजयो वा क्षयो ऽपि वा ।। 7.23.9 ।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ tu yudhyamānānāṃ sāgraḥ saṃvatsaro gataḥ | na cānyatarayostatra vijayo vā kṣayo 'pi vā || 7.23.9 ||
translation: तेषां of them, तु indeed, युध्यमानानां who were fighting, साग्रः more than, संवत्सरः a year, गतः passed, न not, च and, अन्यतरयोः of either of the two, तत्र there, विजयो victory, वा or, क्षयो destruction, अपि even, वा or.
explanation: As they continued to fight, more than a year passed, yet neither side achieved victory nor suffered complete destruction.

shloka_text: ततः पितामहस्तत्र त्रैलोक्यगतिरव्ययः । आजगाम द्रुतं देवो विमानवरमास्थितः ।। 7.23.10 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ pitāmahastatra trailokyagatiravyayaḥ | ājagāma drutaṃ devo vimānavaramāsthitaḥ || 7.23.10 ||
translation: ततः then, पितामहः the grandfather (Brahma), तत्र there, त्रैलोक्यगतिः the resort of the three worlds, अव्ययः the imperishable, आजगाम came, द्रुतं quickly, देवो the god, विमानवरम् on an excellent aerial car, आस्थितः seated.
explanation: Then, the imperishable god Brahma, the lord of the three worlds, quickly arrived there, seated in his magnificent aerial chariot.

shloka_text: निवातकवचानां तु निवार्य रणकर्म तत् । वृद्धः पितामहो वाक्यमुवाच विदितार्थवत् ।। 7.23.11 ।।
transliteration: nivātakavacānāṃ tu nivārya raṇakarma tat | vṛddhaḥ pitāmaho vākyamuvāca viditārthavat || 7.23.11 ||
translation: निवातकवचानां of the Nivatakavachas, तु indeed, निवार्य having stopped, रणकर्म the act of war, तत् that, वृद्धः the old, पितामहः grandfather (Brahma), वाक्यम् words, उवाच spoke, विदितार्थवत् meaningful.
explanation: Having stopped that act of war involving the Nivatakavachas, the wise grandfather Brahma spoke meaningful words.

shloka_text: नह्ययं रावणो युद्धे शक्यो जेतुं सुरासुरैः । न भवन्तः क्षयं नेतुमपि सामरदानवैः ।। 7.23.12 ।।
transliteration: nahyayaṃ rāvaṇo yuddhe śakyo jetuṃ surāsuraiḥ | na bhavantaḥ kṣayaṃ netumapi sāmaradānavaiḥ || 7.23.12 ||
translation: न not, हि indeed, अयं this, रावणो Ravana, युद्धे in battle, शक्यो possible, जेतुं to conquer, सुरासुरैः by gods and asuras, न not, भवन्तः you, क्षयं to destruction, नेतुम् to lead, अपि even, सामरदानवैः by gods and Danavas.
explanation: Indeed, this Ravana cannot be conquered in battle by gods and asuras, nor can you (Nivatakavachas) be led to destruction even by gods and Danavas.

shloka_text: राक्षसस्य सखित्वं च भवद्भिः सह रोचते । अविभक्ताश्च सर्वार्थाः सुहृदां नात्र संशयः ।। 7.23.13 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasasya sakhitvaṃ ca bhavadbhiḥ saha rocate | avibhaktāśca sarvārthāḥ suhṛdāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ || 7.23.13 ||
translation: राक्षसस्य of a Rakshasa, सखित्वं friendship, च and, भवद्भिः with you, सह together, रोचते is pleasing. अविभक्ताः undivided, च and, सर्वार्थाः all interests, सुहृदां of friends, न not, अत्र here, संशयः doubt.
explanation: Friendship with you Rakshasas is agreeable, and there is no doubt that all interests of friends are undivided.

shloka_text: ततो ऽग्निसाक्षिकं सख्यं कृतवांस्तत्र रावणः । निवातकवचैः सार्धं प्रीतिमानभवत्तदा ।। 7.23.14 ।।
transliteration: tato 'gnisākṣikaṃ sakhyaṃ kṛtavāṃstatra rāvaṇaḥ | nivātakavacaiḥ sārdhaṃ prītimānabhavattadā || 7.23.14 ||
translation: ततो then, अग्निसाक्षिकं with fire as witness, सख्यं friendship, कृतवान् made, तत्र there, रावणः Ravana. निवातकवचैः with the Nivātakavachas, सार्धं together with, प्रीतिमान् delighted, अभवत् became, तदा then.
explanation: Then, Ravana established a friendship with the Nivātakavachas, with fire as witness, and became delighted at that time.

shloka_text: अर्थतस्तैर्यथान्यायं संवत्सरमथोषितः । स्वपुरान्निर्विशेषं च प्रियं प्राप्तो दशाननः ।। 7.23.15 ।।
transliteration: arthatastairyathānyāyaṃ saṃvatsaramathoṣitaḥ | svapurānnirviśeṣaṃ ca priyaṃ prāpto daśānanaḥ || 7.23.15 ||
translation: अर्थतः properly, तैः by them, यथान्यायं according to justice, संवत्सरम् for a year, अथ then, उषितः resided. स्वपुरात् from his own city, निर्विशेषं without distinction, च and, प्रियं affection, प्राप्तः obtained, दशाननः Dashanana.
explanation: Ravana then resided there for a year, treated properly and justly by them, receiving affection as if he were in his own city.

shloka_text: ततोपधार्य मायानां शतमेकं समाप्तवान् । सलिलेन्द्रपुरान्वेषी भ्रमति स्म रसातलम् ।। 7.23.16 ।।
transliteration: tatopadhārya māyānāṃ śatamekaṃ samāptavān | salilendrapurānveṣī bhramati sma rasātalam || 7.23.16 ||
translation: ततः then, मायानां of magic arts, शतम् एकं one full hundred, उपधार्य having mastered, समाप्तवान् he completed (learning them), सलिलेन्द्रपुरान्वेषी seeking the city of the lord of waters, रसातलम् in the netherworld, भ्रमति स्म he wandered.
explanation: Then, having mastered a full hundred magic arts, Ravana wandered through the netherworld in search of the city of Varuna, the lord of waters.

shloka_text: ततो ऽश्मनगरं नाम कालकेयैरधिष्ठितम् । गत्वा तु कालकेयांश्च हत्वा तत्र बलोत्कटान् ।। 7.23.17 ।।
transliteration: tato 'śmanagaraṃ nāma kālakeyairadhiṣṭhitam | gatvā tu kālakeyāṃśca hatvā tatra balotkaṭān || 7.23.17 ||
translation: ततो then, अश्मनगरं Ashmanagara, नाम named, कालकेयैः by the Kalakeyas, अधिष्ठितम् inhabited. गत्वा having gone, तु indeed, कालकेयान् the Kalakeyas, च and, हत्वा having killed, तत्र there, बलोत्कटान् the mighty ones.
explanation: Then, having gone to the city named Ashmanagara, which was inhabited by the Kalakeyas, Ravana killed the exceedingly strong Kalakeyas there.

shloka_text: शूर्पणख्याश्च भर्तारमसिना प्राच्छिनत्तदा । श्यालं च बलवन्तं च विद्युज्जिह्वं बलोत्कटम् । जिह्वया संलिहन्तं च राक्षसं समरे तथा ।। 7.23.18 ।।
transliteration: śūrpaṇakhyāśca bhartāramasinā prācchinattadā | śyālaṃ ca balavantaṃ ca vidyujjihvaṃ balotkaṭam | jihvayā saṃlihantaṃ ca rākṣasaṃ samare tathā || 7.23.18 ||
translation: शूर्पणख्याः of Shurpanakha, च and, भर्तारम् husband, असिना with a sword, प्राच्छिनत् cut off, तदा then. श्यालं brother-in-law, च and, बलवन्तं mighty, च and, विद्युज्जिह्वं Vidyujjihva, बलोत्कटम् exceedingly strong. जिह्वया with his tongue, संलिहन्तं licking, च and, राक्षसं Rakshasa, समरे in battle, तथा thus.
explanation: Then, Ravana cut off Shurpanakha's husband, his mighty and exceedingly strong brother-in-law named Vidyujjihva, who was a Rakshasa licking (blood/wounds) with his tongue in battle, with his sword.

shloka_text: तं विजित्य मुहूर्तेन जघ्ने दैत्यांश्चतुःशतम् ।। 7.23.19 ।।
transliteration: taṃ vijitya muhūrtena jaghne daityāṃścatuḥśatam || 7.23.19 ||
translation: तम् him, विजित्य having conquered, मुहूर्तेन in a moment, जघ्ने he killed, दैत्यान् demons, चतुःशतम् four hundred,
explanation: Having conquered him, he killed four hundred demons in an instant.

shloka_text: ततः पाण्डुरमेघाभं कैलासमिव भास्वरम् । वरुणस्यालयं दिव्यमपश्यद्राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.23.20 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ pāṇḍurameghābhaṃ kailāsamiva bhāsvaram | varuṇasyālayaṃ divyamapaśyadrākṣasādhipaḥ || 7.23.20 ||
translation: ततः then, पाण्डुरमेघाभम् resembling white clouds, कैलासमिव like Mount Kailasa, भास्वरम् shining, वरुणस्य of Varuna, आलयम् abode, दिव्यम् divine, अपश्यत् he saw, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of rakshasas,
explanation: Then, the lord of rakshasas saw the divine abode of Varuna, which resembled white clouds and shone like Mount Kailasa.

shloka_text: क्षरन्तीं च पयस्तत्र सुरभिं गामवस्थिताम् । यस्याः पयोभिनिष्यन्दात्क्षीरोदो नाम सागरः ।। 7.23.21 ।।
transliteration: kṣarantīṃ ca payastatra surabhiṃ gāmavasthitām | yasyāḥ payobhiniṣyandātkṣīrodo nāma sāgaraḥ || 7.23.21 ||
translation: क्षरन्तीम् flowing, च and, पयः milk, तत्र there, सुरभिम् Surabhi, गाम् cow, अवस्थिताम् standing, यस्याः from whose, पयोभिनिष्यन्दात् from the flowing of milk, क्षीरोदः Kshiroda, नाम named, सागरः ocean,
explanation: There he saw the divine cow Surabhi, standing and continuously flowing milk, from whose abundant milk flow the ocean named Kshiroda originated.

shloka_text: ददर्श रावणस्तत्र गोवृषेन्द्रवरारणिम् । यस्माच्चन्द्रः प्रभवति शीतरश्मिर्निशाकरः ।। 7.23.22 ।।
transliteration: dadarśa rāvaṇastatra govṛṣendravarāraṇim | yasmāccandraḥ prabhavati śītaraśmirniśākaraḥ || 7.23.22 ||
translation: ददर्श he saw, रावणः Ravana, तत्र there, गोवृषेन्द्रवरारणिम् the best source of cows, bulls, and excellent things, यस्मात् from which, चन्द्रः the moon, प्रभवति originates, शीतरश्मिः cool-rayed, निशाकरः night-maker,
explanation: There Ravana saw the ocean, the best source of cows, bulls, and excellent things, from which the cool-rayed moon, the maker of night, originated.

shloka_text: यं समाश्रित्य जीवन्ति फेनपाः परमर्षयः । अमृतं यत्र चोत्पन्नं स्वधा च स्वधभोजिनाम् ।। 7.23.23 ।।
transliteration: yaṃ samāśritya jīvanti phenapāḥ paramarṣayaḥ | amṛtaṃ yatra cotpannaṃ svadhā ca svadhabhojinām || 7.23.23 ||
translation: यम् which, समाश्रित्य depending on, जीवन्ति live, फेनपाः foam-drinkers, परमर्षयः great sages, अमृतम् nectar, यत्र where, च and, उत्पन्नम् originated, स्वधा Svadhā, च and, स्वधभोजिनाम् for those who partake of Svadhā,
explanation: Great sages known as foam-drinkers subsist by depending on this ocean, and it is also where nectar and Svadhā, the offering for ancestors, originated.

shloka_text: यां ब्रुवन्ति नरा लोके सुरभिं नाम नामतः । प्रदक्षिणं तु तां कृत्वा रावणः परमाद्भुताम् ।। 7.23.24 ।।
transliteration: yāṃ bruvanti narā loke surabhiṃ nāma nāmataḥ | pradakṣiṇaṃ tu tāṃ kṛtvā rāvaṇaḥ paramādbhutām || 7.23.24 ||
translation: यां which, ब्रुवन्ति call, नरा men, लोके in the world, सुरभिं Surabhi, नाम by name, नामतः by name, प्रदक्षिणं circumambulation, तु indeed, तां her, कृत्वा having done, रावणः Ravana, परमाद्भुताम् exceedingly wonderful,
explanation: Ravana, having circumambulated the exceedingly wonderful Surabhi, whom people in the world call by that name, then proceeded.

shloka_text: प्रविवेश महाघोरं गुप्तं बहुविधैर्बलैः । ततो धाराशताकीर्णं शारदाभ्रनिभं तदा । नित्यप्रहृष्टं ददृशे वरुणस्य गृहोत्तमम् ।। 7.23.25 ।।
transliteration: praviveśa mahāghoraṃ guptaṃ bahuvidhairbalaiḥ | tato dhārāśatākīrṇaṃ śāradābhranibhaṃ tadā | nityaprahṛṣṭaṃ dadṛśe varuṇasya gṛhottamam || 7.23.25 ||
translation: प्रविवेश entered, महाघोरं very dreadful, गुप्तं guarded, बहुविधैर्बलैः by various kinds of forces, ततो then, धाराशताकीर्णं filled with hundreds of streams, शारदाभ्रनिभं resembling an autumn cloud, तदा then, नित्यप्रहृष्टं always joyful, ददृशे he saw, वरुणस्य of Varuna, गृहोत्तमम् the excellent house,
explanation: He then entered a very dreadful place, guarded by various forces, and there he saw Varuna's excellent abode, which was filled with hundreds of streams, resembled an autumn cloud, and was always joyful.

shloka_text: ततो हत्वा बलाध्यक्षान्समरे तैश्च ताडितः । अब्रवीच्च ततो योधान्राजा शीघ्रं निवेद्यताम् ।। 7.23.26 ।।
transliteration: tato hatvā balādhyakṣānsamare taiśca tāḍitaḥ | abravīcca tato yodhānrājā śīghraṃ nivedyatām || 7.23.26 ||
translation: ततो then, हत्वा having killed, बलाध्यक्षान् the commanders of the army, समरे in battle, तैश्च and by them, ताडितः struck, अब्रवीच्च and he said, ततो then, योधान् to the warriors, राजा the king, शीघ्रं quickly, निवेद्यताम् let it be announced,
explanation: Then, having killed the commanders of the army in battle and being struck by them, Ravana said to the warriors, "Let the king (Varuna) be quickly informed."

shloka_text: युद्धार्थी रावणः प्राप्तस्तस्य युद्धं प्रदीयताम् । वद वा न भयं ते ऽस्ति निर्जितो ऽस्मीति साञ्जलिः ।। 7.23.27 ।।
transliteration: yuddhārthī rāvaṇaḥ prāptastasya yuddhaṃ pradīyatām | vada vā na bhayaṃ te 'sti nirjito 'smīti sāñjaliḥ || 7.23.27 ||
translation: युद्धार्थी desirous of battle, रावणः Ravana, प्राप्तः has arrived, तस्य to him, युद्धं battle, प्रदीयताम् let it be given, वद or say, वा or, न not, भयं fear, ते to you, अस्ति is, निर्जितो conquered, अस्मि I am, इति thus, साञ्जलिः with folded hands,
explanation: "Ravana, desirous of battle, has arrived; let battle be given to him, or else, with folded hands, say 'I am conquered' if you have no fear."

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे क्रुद्धा वरुणस्य महात्मनः । पुत्राः पौत्राश्च निष्क्रामन्गौश्च पुष्कर एव च ।। 7.23.28 ।।
transliteration: etasminnantare kruddhā varuṇasya mahātmanaḥ | putrāḥ pautrāśca niṣkrāmangauśca puṣkara eva ca || 7.23.28 ||
translation: एतस्मिन् at this, अन्तरे moment, क्रुद्धा enraged, वरुणस्य of Varuna, महात्मनः the great-souled, पुत्राः sons, पौत्राश्च and grandsons, निष्क्रामन् came out, गौश्च and Gau, पुष्कर Pushkara, एव indeed, च and,
explanation: At this moment, the enraged sons and grandsons of the great-souled Varuna, including Gau and Pushkara, came out.

shloka_text: ते तु वीर्यगुणोपेता बलैः परिवृताः स्वकैः । युङ्क्त्वा रथान्कामगमानुद्यद्भास्वरवर्चसः ।। 7.23.29 ।।
transliteration: te tu vīryaguṇopetā balaiḥ parivṛtāḥ svakaiḥ | yuṅktvā rathānkāmagamānudyadbhāsvaravarcasaḥ || 7.23.29 ||
translation: ते they, तु indeed, वीर्यगुणोपेताः endowed with valorous qualities, बलैः by forces, परिवृताः surrounded, स्वकैः their own, युङ्क्त्वा having yoked, रथान् chariots, कामगमान् moving at will, उद्यद्भास्वरवर्चसः with rising brilliant splendor,
explanation: Endowed with valorous qualities and surrounded by their own forces, they yoked their chariots, which moved at will, shining with brilliant splendor.

shloka_text: ततो युद्धं समभवद्दारुणं रोमहर्षणम् । सलिलेन्द्रस्य पुत्राणां रावणस्य च धीमतः ।। 7.23.30 ।।
transliteration: tato yuddhaṃ samabhavaddāruṇaṃ romaharṣaṇam | salilendrasya putrāṇāṃ rāvaṇasya ca dhīmataḥ || 7.23.30 ||
translation: ततः then, युद्धम् battle, समभवत् occurred, दारुणम् terrible, रोमहर्षणम् hair-raising, सलिलेन्द्रस्य of the lord of waters, पुत्राणाम् of the sons, रावणस्य of Ravana, च and, धीमतः intelligent,
explanation: Then, a terrible and hair-raising battle ensued between the sons of Varuna, the lord of waters, and the intelligent Ravana.

shloka_text: अमात्यैश्च महावीर्यैर्दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः । वारुणं तद्बलं कृत्स्नं क्षणेन विनिपातितम् ।। 7.23.31 ।।
transliteration: amātyaiśca mahāvīryairdaśagrīvasya rakṣasaḥ | vāruṇaṃ tadbalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ kṣaṇena vinipātitam || 7.23.31 ||
translation: अमात्यैः by ministers, च and, महावीर्यैः very powerful, दशग्रीवस्य of Dashagriva, रक्षसः the Rakshasa, वारुणम् belonging to Varuna, तत् that, बलम् army, कृत्स्नम् entire, क्षणेन in a moment, विनिपातितम् was destroyed,
explanation: And by the very powerful ministers of the Rakshasa Dashagriva, that entire army of Varuna was destroyed in a moment.

shloka_text: समीक्ष्य स्वबलं सङ्ख्ये वरुणस्य सुतास्तदा । अर्दिताः शरजालेन निवृत्ता रणकर्मणः ।। 7.23.32 ।।
transliteration: samīkṣya svabalaṃ saṅkhye varuṇasya sutāstadā | arditāḥ śarajālena nivṛttā raṇakarmaṇaḥ || 7.23.32 ||
translation: समीक्ष्य having seen, स्वबलम् their own army, सङ्ख्ये in battle, वरुणस्य of Varuna, सुताः sons, तदा then, अर्दिताः afflicted, शरजालेन by a shower of arrows, निवृत्ताः retreated, रणकर्मणः from the act of battle,
explanation: Then, seeing their own army afflicted by a shower of arrows in battle, the sons of Varuna retreated from the fight.

shloka_text: महीतलगतास्ते तु रावणं दृश्य पुष्पके । आकाशमाशु विविशुः स्यन्दनैः शीघ्रगामिभिः ।। 7.23.33 ।।
transliteration: mahītalagatāste tu rāvaṇaṃ dṛśya puṣpake | ākāśamāśu viviśuḥ syandanaiḥ śīghragāmibhiḥ || 7.23.33 ||
translation: महीतलगताः situated on the ground, ते they, तु indeed, रावणम् Ravana, दृश्य having seen, पुष्पके in the Pushpaka (chariot), आकाशम् sky, आशु quickly, विविशुः entered, स्यन्दनैः by chariots, शीघ्रगामिभिः swift-moving,
explanation: Indeed, they, who were on the ground, having seen Ravana in the Pushpaka chariot, quickly ascended into the sky with their swift-moving chariots.

shloka_text: महादासीत्ततस्तेषां तुल्यं स्थानमवाप्य तत् । आकाशयुद्धं तुमुलं देवदानवयोरिव ।। 7.23.34 ।।
transliteration: mahādāsīttatasteṣāṃ tulyaṃ sthānamavāpya tat | ākāśayuddhaṃ tumulaṃ devadānavayoriva || 7.23.34 ||
translation: महादासीत् it was great, ततस्तेषां then for them, तुल्यं equal, स्थानमवाप्य having obtained a place, तत् that, आकाशयुद्धं sky-battle, तुमुलं tumultuous, देवदानवयोरिव like that of gods and demons.
explanation: After obtaining an equal position in the sky, a great and tumultuous battle ensued among them, resembling the fierce combat between gods and demons.

shloka_text: ततस्ते रावणं युद्धे शरैः पावकसन्निभैः । विमुखीकृत्य सन्तुष्टा विनेदुर्विविधान्रवान् ।। 7.23.35 ।।
transliteration: tataste rāvaṇaṃ yuddhe śaraiḥ pāvakasannibhaiḥ | vimukhīkṛtya santuṣṭā vinedurvividhānravān || 7.23.35 ||
translation: ततस्ते then they, रावणं Ravana, युद्धे in battle, शरैः with arrows, पावकसन्निभैः resembling fire, विमुखीकृत्य having turned away, सन्तुष्टा satisfied, विनेदुर्विविधान्रवान् they roared various sounds.
explanation: Then, having turned Ravana away in battle with their fire-like arrows, they were satisfied and roared various sounds.

shloka_text: ततो महोदरः क्रुद्धो राजानं दृश्य धर्षितम् । त्यक्त्वा मृत्युभयं वीरो युद्धकाङ्क्षी व्यलोकयत् ।। 7.23.36 ।।
transliteration: tato mahodaraḥ kruddho rājānaṃ dṛśya dharṣitam | tyaktvā mṛtyubhayaṃ vīro yuddhakāṅkṣī vyalokayat || 7.23.36 ||
translation: ततो then, महोदरः Mahodara, क्रुद्धो enraged, राजानं the king, दृश्य having seen, धर्षितम् humiliated, त्यक्त्वा having abandoned, मृत्युभयं fear of death, वीरो the hero, युद्धकाङ्क्षी desirous of battle, व्यलोकयत् he looked (at the enemy).
explanation: Then, the enraged hero Mahodara, seeing his king humiliated, abandoned all fear of death and, desirous of battle, looked towards the enemy.

shloka_text: तेन ते दारुणा युद्धे कामगाः पवनोपमाः । महोदरेण गदया हता वै प्रययुः क्षितिम् ।। 7.23.37 ।।
transliteration: tena te dāruṇā yuddhe kāmagāḥ pavanopamāḥ | mahodareṇa gadayā hatā vai prayayuḥ kṣitim || 7.23.37 ||
translation: तेन by him, ते those, दारुणा fierce, युद्धे in battle, कामगाः moving at will, पवनोपमाः resembling wind, महोदरेण by Mahodara, गदया with a mace, हता struck, वै indeed, प्रययुः they went, क्षितिम् to the earth.
explanation: In that fierce battle, those who moved at will and resembled the wind were indeed struck by Mahodara with his mace and fell to the earth.

shloka_text: तेषां वरुणपुत्राणां हत्वा योधान्हयाञ्छतान् । मुमोचाशु महानादं विरथान्प्रेक्ष्य तान्स्थितान् ।। 7.23.38 ।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ varuṇaputrāṇāṃ hatvā yodhānhayāñchatān | mumocāśu mahānādaṃ virathānprekṣya tānsthitān || 7.23.38 ||
translation: तेषां of them, वरुणपुत्राणां of the sons of Varuna, हत्वा having killed, योधान्हयाञ्छतान् hundreds of warriors and horses, मुमोचाशु quickly he let out, महानादं a great roar, विरथान्प्रेक्ष्य having seen them chariot-less, तान्स्थितान् standing.
explanation: Having killed hundreds of warriors and horses belonging to the sons of Varuna, Mahodara quickly let out a great roar upon seeing them standing dismounted from their chariots.

shloka_text: ते तु तेषां रथाः साश्वाः सह सारथिभिर्हतैः । महोदरेण निहताः पतिताः पृथिवीतले ।। 7.23.39 ।।
transliteration: te tu teṣāṃ rathāḥ sāśvāḥ saha sārathibhirhataiḥ | mahodareṇa nihatāḥ patitāḥ pṛthivītale || 7.23.39 ||
translation: ते those, तु indeed, तेषां their, रथाः chariots, साश्वाः with horses, सह along with, सारथिभिः charioteers, हतैः killed, महोदरेण by Mahodara, निहताः struck down, पतिताः fell, पृथिवीतले on the ground
explanation: Mahodara struck down their chariots, which, along with their horses and slain charioteers, fell to the ground.

shloka_text: ते तु त्यक्त्वा रथान्पुत्रा वरुणस्य महात्मनः । आकाशे विष्ठिताः शूराः स्वप्रभावान्न विव्यथुः ।। 7.23.40 ।।
transliteration: te tu tyaktvā rathānputrā varuṇasya mahātmanaḥ | ākāśe viṣṭhitāḥ śūrāḥ svaprabhāvānna vivyathuḥ || 7.23.40 ||
translation: ते those, तु but, त्यक्त्वा having abandoned, रथान् chariots, पुत्राः sons, वरुणस्य of Varuna, महात्मनः the great-souled, आकाशे in the sky, विष्ठिताः stood, शूराः brave ones, स्वप्रभावात् due to their own power, न not, विव्यथुः were distressed
explanation: But those brave sons of the great-souled Varuna, having abandoned their chariots, stood in the sky and were not distressed due to their inherent power.

shloka_text: धनूंषि कृत्वा सज्जानि विनिर्भिद्य महोदरम् । रावणं समरे क्रुद्धाः सहिताः समभिद्रवन् ।। 7.23.41 ।।
transliteration: dhanūṃṣi kṛtvā sajjāni vinirbhidya mahodaram | rāvaṇaṃ samare kruddhāḥ sahitāḥ samabhidravan || 7.23.41 ||
translation: धनूंषि bows, कृत्वा having made, सज्जानि ready, विनिर्भिद्य having pierced, महोदरम् Mahodara, रावणं Ravana, समरे in battle, क्रुद्धाः enraged, सहिताः together, समभिद्रवन् attacked
explanation: Enraged, they made their bows ready, pierced Mahodara, and together attacked Ravana in battle.

shloka_text: सायकैश्चापविभ्रष्टैर्वज्रकल्पैः सुदारुणैः । दारयन्ति स्म सङ्क्रुद्धा मेघा इव महागिरिम् ।। 7.23.42 ।।
transliteration: sāyakaiścāpavibhraṣṭairvajrakalpaiḥ sudāruṇaiḥ | dārayanti sma saṅkruddhā meghā iva mahāgirim || 7.23.42 ||
translation: सायकैः with arrows, च and, आपविभ्रष्टैः released from bows, वज्रकल्पैः like thunderbolts, सुदारुणैः very terrible, दारयन्ति स्म they tore apart, सङ्क्रुद्धाः greatly enraged, मेघाः clouds, इव like, महागिरिम् a great mountain
explanation: Greatly enraged, they tore him apart with very terrible arrows, released from their bows and resembling thunderbolts, just as clouds tear apart a great mountain.

shloka_text: ततः क्रुद्धो दशग्रीवः कालाग्निरिव निर्गतः । शरवर्षैर्महाघोरैस्तेषां मर्मस्वताडयत् ।। 7.23.43 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ kruddho daśagrīvaḥ kālāgniriva nirgataḥ | śaravarṣairmahāghoraisteṣāṃ marmasvatāḍayat || 7.23.43 ||
translation: ततः then, क्रुद्धः enraged, दशग्रीवः the ten-necked (Ravana), कालाग्निः the fire of destruction, इव like, निर्गतः emerged, शरवर्षैः with showers of arrows, महाघोरैः very dreadful, तेषां their, मर्मसु vital spots, अताडयत् struck
explanation: Then, the enraged Ravana, appearing like the fire of destruction, struck their vital spots with very dreadful showers of arrows.

shloka_text: ततस्तेनैव सहसा सीदन्ति स्म पदातयः । मुसलानि विचित्राणि ततो भल्लशतानि च ।। 7.23.44 ।।
transliteration: tatastenaiva sahasā sīdanti sma padātayaḥ | musalāni vicitrāṇi tato bhallaśatāni ca || 7.23.44 ||
translation: ततः then, तेनैव by him alone, सहसा suddenly, सीदन्ति स्म were sinking, पदातयः the foot-soldiers, मुसलानि maces, विचित्राणि various, ततः then, भल्लशतानि hundreds of spears, च and.
explanation: Then, by him alone, the foot-soldiers suddenly began to collapse under the impact of various maces and hundreds of spears.

shloka_text: पट्टिशांश्चैव शक्तीश्च शतघ्नीस्तोमरांस्तथा । पातयामास दुर्धर्षस्तेषामुपरि विष्ठितः ।। 7.23.45 ।।
transliteration: paṭṭiśāṃścaiva śaktīśca śataghnīstomarāṃstathā | pātayāmāsa durdharṣasteṣāmupari viṣṭhitaḥ || 7.23.45 ||
translation: पट्टिशान् sharp-edged spears, च and, एव indeed, शक्तीः lances, च and, शतघ्नीः 'hundred-killers' (a type of weapon), तोमरान् javelins, तथा and also, पातयामास he hurled, दुर्धर्षः the irresistible one (Ravana), तेषाम् upon them, उपरि above, विष्ठितः standing.
explanation: The irresistible Ravana, positioned above them, hurled down sharp-edged spears, lances, 'hundred-killers', and javelins upon them.

shloka_text: अपविद्धास्तु ते वीरा विनिष्पेतुः पदातयः । महापङ्कमिवासाद्य कुञ्जराष्षष्टिहायनाः ।। 7.23.46 ।।
transliteration: apaviddhāstu te vīrā viniṣpetuḥ padātayaḥ | mahāpaṅkamivāsādya kuñjarāṣṣaṣṭihāyanāḥ || 7.23.46 ||
translation: अपविद्धाः struck down, तु but, ते those, वीराः brave ones, विनिष्पेतुः they fled, पदातयः the foot-soldiers, महापङ्कम् a great mud-pit, इव like, आसाद्य having fallen into, कुञ्जराः elephants, षष्टिहायनाः sixty years old.
explanation: Those brave foot-soldiers, struck down, scattered and fled like sixty-year-old elephants that have fallen into a deep mud-pit.

shloka_text: सीदमानान्सुतान्दृष्ट्वा विह्वलान्सुमहौजसः । ननाद रावणो हर्षान्महानम्बुधरो यथा ।। 7.23.47 ।।
transliteration: sīdamānānsutāndṛṣṭvā vihvalānsumahaujasaḥ | nanāda rāvaṇo harṣānmahānambudharo yathā || 7.23.47 ||
translation: सीदमानान् sinking, सुतान् sons (enemies), दृष्ट्वा having seen, विह्वलान् distressed, सुमहौजसः very mighty ones, ननाद roared, रावणः Ravana, हर्षात् from joy, महान् a great, अम्बुधरः cloud, यथा like.
explanation: Seeing his very mighty enemies (literally 'sons') collapsing and distressed, Ravana roared with joy like a great thundercloud.

shloka_text: ततो रक्षो महानादान्मुक्त्वा हन्ति स्म वारुणान् । नानाप्रहरणोपेतैर्धारापातैरिवाम्बुदः ।। 7.23.48 ।।
transliteration: tato rakṣo mahānādānmuktvā hanti sma vāruṇān | nānāpraharaṇopetairdhārāpātairivāmbudaḥ || 7.23.48 ||
translation: ततः then, रक्षः the Rakshasa (Ravana), महानादान् great roars, मुक्त्वा having uttered, हन्ति स्म he struck, वारुणान् the followers of Varuna (Devas), नानाप्रहरणोपेतैः with various weapons, धारापातैः with torrents of rain (showers of weapons), इव like, अम्बुदः a cloud.
explanation: Then, the Rakshasa Ravana, having uttered great roars, struck down the followers of Varuna (Devas) with showers of various weapons, just like a cloud pours down torrents of rain.

shloka_text: ततस्ते विमुखाः सर्वे पतिता धरणीतले । रणात्स्वपुरुषैः शीघ्रं गृहाण्येव प्रवेशिताः ।। 7.23.49 ।।
transliteration: tataste vimukhāḥ sarve patitā dharaṇītale | raṇātsvapuruṣaiḥ śīghraṃ gṛhāṇyeva praveśitāḥ || 7.23.49 ||
translation: ततः then, ते they, विमुखाः turned away (defeated), सर्वे all, पतिताः fallen, धरणीतले on the ground, रणात् from the battle, स्वपुरुषैः by their own men, शीघ्रं quickly, गृहाणि into their homes, एव indeed, प्रवेशिताः were brought.
explanation: Then, all of them, defeated and fallen to the ground, were quickly brought back into their homes by their own men from the battlefield.

shloka_text: तानब्रवीत्ततो रक्षो वरुणाय निवेद्यताम् ।। 7.23.50 ।।
transliteration: tānabravīttato rakṣo varuṇāya nivedyatām || 7.23.50 ||
translation: तान् to them, अब्रवीत् said, ततः then, रक्षो the demon (Ravana), वरुणाय to Varuna, निवेद्यताम् let it be announced.
explanation: Then the demon Ravana said to them, "Let this be announced to Varuna."

shloka_text: रावणं त्वब्रवीन्मन्त्री प्रहस्तो (प्रहसो) नाम वारुणः । गतः खलु महाराजो ब्रह्मलोकं जलेश्वरः ।। 7.23.51 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇaṃ tvabravīnmantrī prahasto (prahaso) nāma vāruṇaḥ | gataḥ khalu mahārājo brahmalokaṃ jaleśvaraḥ || 7.23.51 ||
translation: रावणं to Ravana, तु indeed, अब्रवीत् said, मन्त्री the minister, प्रहस्तो Prahasta, नाम named, वारुणः of Varuna, गतः gone, खलु indeed, महाराजो the great king, ब्रह्मलोकं to the world of Brahma, जलेश्वरः the lord of waters (Varuna).
explanation: Then a minister of Varuna named Prahasta (or Prahasa) said to Ravana, "Indeed, the great king, the lord of waters Varuna, has gone to the world of Brahma."

shloka_text: गान्धर्वं वरुणः श्रोतुं यं त्वमाह्वयसे युधि । तत्किं तव वृथा वीर परिश्रम्य गते नृपे । ये तु सन्निहिता वीराः कुमारास्ते पराजिताः ।। 7.23.52 ।।
transliteration: gāndharvaṃ varuṇaḥ śrotuṃ yaṃ tvamāhvayase yudhi | tatkiṃ tava vṛthā vīra pariśramya gate nṛpe | ye tu sannihitā vīrāḥ kumārāste parājitāḥ || 7.23.52 ||
translation: गान्धर्वं Gandharva (music/art), वरुणः Varuna, श्रोतुं to hear, यं whom, त्वं you, आह्वयसे challenge, युधि in battle, तत् therefore, किं what (is the use), तव your, वृथा in vain, वीर O hero, परिश्रम्य having exerted, गते when gone, नृपे the king; ये those who, तु but, सन्निहिताः present, वीराः heroes, कुमाराः princes, ते they, पराजिताः defeated.
explanation: Varuna, whom you challenge in battle, has gone to hear Gandharva music; therefore, O hero, what is the use of your vain exertion when the king is absent, and those princes who were present here have already been defeated?

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः । हर्षान्नादं विमुञ्चन्वै निष्क्रान्तो वरुणालयात् ।। 7.23.53 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasendrastu tacchrutvā nāma viśrāvya cātmanaḥ | harṣānnādaṃ vimuñcanvai niṣkrānto varuṇālayāt || 7.23.53 ||
translation: राक्षसेन्द्रः the lord of demons (Ravana), तु indeed, तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, नाम name, विश्राव्य having proclaimed, च and, आत्मनः his own, हर्षात् from joy, नादं a roar, विमुञ्चन् releasing, वै indeed, निष्क्रान्तः departed, वरुणालयात् from Varuna's abode.
explanation: Having heard that, the lord of demons Ravana, proclaiming his own name and uttering a joyful roar, indeed departed from Varuna's abode.

shloka_text: आगतस्तु पथा येन तेनैव विनिवृत्य सः । लङ्कामभिमुखो रक्षो नभस्तलगतो ययौ ।। 7.23.54 ।।
transliteration: āgatastu pathā yena tenaiva vinivṛtya saḥ | laṅkāmabhimukho rakṣo nabhastalagato yayau || 7.23.54 ||
translation: आगतस्तु having come, पथा by the path, येन by which, तेनैव by that very, विनिवृत्य having returned, सः he, लङ्कामभिमुखो facing Lanka, रक्षो the demon, नभस्तलगतो moving in the sky, ययौ went.
explanation: Having arrived by a certain path, the demon Ravana returned by that very path, flying through the sky towards Lanka. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रयोविंशः सर्गः ।। 23 ।। Thus ends the twenty-third sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
